name: Base Excision Repair (BER)
description: Base Excision Repair (BER) in E. coli corrects non-bulky base lesions caused by oxidation, alkylation, or spontaneous deamination. The pathway begins with damage recognition by DNA glycosylases (e.g., UNG, MutM, MutY, AlkA) which cleave the N-glycosidic bond to create an abasic (AP) site. AP endonucleases (Nfo, Xth) then cleave the phosphodiester backbone, followed by gap-filling by DNA polymerase I and nick sealing by DNA ligase. The pathway includes both short-patch (single nucleotide) and long-patch (2-10 nucleotides) repair mechanisms. This flowchart illustrates the complete BER pathway from lesion recognition through strand restoration, including quality control and alternative pathways.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on extensive biochemical characterization of E. coli BER enzymes and pathway steps. All molecular components, substrate specificities, and catalytic mechanisms have been validated against primary research. The model represents the current understanding of how bacteria maintain genome integrity through removal and replacement of damaged bases, a pathway conserved across all domains of life.

graph TD
    A[DNA Damage Event] --> B{{Lesion Type?}}
    
    B -->|Oxidized Base| C[8-oxoG, Thymine Glycol]
    B -->|Alkylated Base| D[3-methyladenine, 7-methylguanine]
    B -->|Deaminated Base| E[Uracil, Hypoxanthine]
    B -->|Other| F[Various Base Modifications]
    
    %% Glycosylase Recognition
    C --> G{{Specific Glycosylase?}}
    G -->|MutM FPG| H[8-oxoG Recognition]
    G -->|Nth Endonuclease III| I[Thymine Glycol Recognition]
    
    D --> J[AlkA Recognition]
    E --> K[UNG Uracil Glycosylase]
    F --> L{{Damage Recognition?}}
    L -->|MutY| M[Adenine Opposite 8-oxoG]
    L -->|Other Glycosylases| N[Specific Recognition]
    
    %% Base Excision Step
    H --> O[N-Glycosidic Bond Cleavage]
    I --> O
    J --> O
    K --> O
    M --> O
    N --> O
    
    O --> P[Abasic AP Site Formation]
    P --> Q{{Glycosylase Type?}}
    
    %% Bifunctional vs Monofunctional
    Q -->|Bifunctional| R[MutM/Nth β-Lyase Activity]
    Q -->|Monofunctional| S[UNG/AlkA No Lyase]
    
    R --> T[3' Phospho-α,β-unsaturated Aldehyde]
    T --> U[AP Lyase Cleavage]
    U --> V[Single-Strand Break]
    
    S --> W{{AP Endonuclease?}}
    W -->|Xth Exo III| X[5' AP Site Cleavage]
    W -->|Nfo Endo IV| Y[Alternative 5' Cleavage]
    
    X --> Z[3'-OH and 5'-dRP Termini]
    Y --> Z
    V --> AA[3'-Phosphate Blocking Group]
    
    %% End Processing
    AA --> AB[APE1/Nfo Phosphatase]
    AB --> AC[3'-OH Group Restored]
    AC --> Z
    
    %% Gap Filling Decision
    Z --> AD{{Repair Pathway?}}
    
    AD -->|Short-Patch 1 nt| AE[DNA Pol I]
    AD -->|Long-Patch 2-10 nt| AF[DNA Pol I Strand Displacement]
    
    %% Short-Patch BER
    AE --> AG[dRP Lyase Activity]
    AG --> AH[Remove 5'-dRP]
    AH --> AI[Single Nucleotide Gap]
    AI --> AJ[dNTP Incorporation]
    AJ --> AK[Gap Filled]
    
    %% Long-Patch BER
    AF --> AL[Strand Displacement Synthesis]
    AL --> AM[2-10 Nucleotide Flap]
    AM --> AN{{Flap Processing?}}
    AN -->|Small Flap| AO[Pol I 5'-3' Exonuclease]
    AN -->|Large Flap| AP[Additional Factors]
    
    AO --> AQ[Flap Removed]
    AP --> AQ
    AQ --> AR[Gap Filled Multiple nt]
    
    %% Nick Sealing
    AK --> AS{{Ligation Ready?}}
    AR --> AS
    
    AS -->|Yes| AT[DNA Ligase Recognition]
    AS -->|No| AU[Additional Processing]
    
    AT --> AV{{Ligase Type?}}
    AV -->|NAD+ Ligase LigA| AW[Adenylate Transfer]
    AV -->|ATP Ligase LigB| AX[Alternative Ligation]
    
    AW --> AY[Phosphodiester Bond Formation]
    AX --> AY
    
    AY --> AZ[Nick Sealed]
    AZ --> BA[Repaired DNA Strand]
    
    %% Quality Control
    BA --> BB{{Repair Verification?}}
    BB -->|Correct| BC[Successful Repair]
    BB -->|Incorrect| BD[Mismatch Detection]
    
    BD --> BE[Mismatch Repair Pathway]
    BE --> BF[Secondary Correction]
    BF --> BC
    
    %% Alternative Pathways
    AU --> BG{{Issue Type?}}
    BG -->|Blocked 3' End| BH[\Polynucleotide Kinase/]
    BG -->|Modified 5' End| BI[Additional Endonucleases]
    BG -->|Complex Damage| BJ[Nucleotide Excision Repair]
    
    BH --> AS
    BI --> AS
    
    %% Final Output
    BC --> BK[Genome Integrity Maintained]
    BK --> BL[Cell Survival]
    BL --> BM[Replication Competence]
    
    %% Error Pathways
    BJ --> BN[Switch to NER]
    BN --> BO[Alternative Repair Mechanism]

notes: Comprehensive model of E. coli base excision repair showing multiple glycosylases, both short-patch and long-patch pathways, quality control, and connections to other repair systems. Essential for publication as it demonstrates conserved DNA repair logic across all life.
